title: Crypto

8.name: Hardcoded Plaintext Password
8.vuln: Can gain access by reading source code.

13.name: Weak encryption/hashing
13.vuln: Unsalted MD5 hashes are easily reversible.

27.name: RCE via eval()
27.vuln: eval() executes arbitrary input as code, allowing full system compromise.

title: Deserializer

15.name: Prototype Pollution
15.vuln: Using lodash.merge with unsanitized user input allows an attacker to inject properties like '__proto__.role' into the global Object prototype, elevating privileges for all objects.

18.name: Path Traversal (LFI)
18.vuln: The theme parameter is used in a file path without sanitization. An attacker can use '../' sequences to read sensitive system files like /etc/passwd.

29.name: Blind OS Command Injection
29.vuln: The callback variable is concatenated directly into a shell command string. An attacker can use shell metacharacters like ';' or '&&' to execute arbitrary OS commands.

title: Propagator

10.name: Server-Side Template Injection (Function Constructor)
10.vuln: The status parameter is string-interpolated into a 'new Function' body. While it looks like a simple object return, an attacker can break out of the string literal using "', ...}" syntax to execute arbitrary JavaScript within the process context.

16.name: V8 Deserialization Vulnerability
16.vuln: Unlike JSON.parse, the v8.deserialize API can reconstruct complex objects. An attacker can provide a base64-encoded Buffer that, when deserialized, executes code or manipulates internal object states that Object.assign later propagates.

25.name: VM Sandbox Escape
25.vuln: The 'vm' module in Node.js is not a security sandbox. Since the 'config' object (globalConfig) is passed into the context, an attacker can use 'config.constructor.constructor("return process")()' to access the main process and execute OS-level commands.

title: Bypass

1.name: Weak Security Check
1.vuln: The system only checks if url starts with file://, but an attacker can use URL encoding to bypass a simple prefix check, which could lead to SSRF if the conversion logic doesnt have a hardened sandbox.

8.name: SSL Validation Bypass
8.vuln: If the conversion function is configured to ignore SSL errors it completely disables chain of trust, which could facilitate a MITM attack between the PDF engine and sygris.com and inject malicious HTML/JS into PDF generation process

18.name: Information Disclosure
18.vuln: res.logs is being converted to a string for validation, but in many PDF conversion libraries logs can include console output from the remote site, internal file paths, or leaked memory fragments. If logs are exposed to user or saved in an insecure location is a significant Information Disclosure vulnerability

title: Hijack

5.name: Predictable Session Identifiers (IDOR)
5.vuln: The sessionId is constructed via simple string concatenation of predictable values. If an attacker knows the meetingId and a target's userId, they can pre-calculate the session string to hijack or spoof a user's presence.

6.name: Authentication Bypass via setUserId
6.vuln: By passing an unvalidated, predictable string to this.setUserId(), the application effectively 'logs in' the connection as that string. This bypasses formal authentication and allows an attacker to assume any identity the system recognizes in that format.

8.name: Unauthenticated Resource Exhaustion
8.vuln: The logic creates a 'dummy' record for any non-existent user before validating the token. An attacker can flood the database with garbage records by iterating through random userIDs, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) or database pollution.

title: DOM

7.name: DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
7.vuln: Directly concatenating the 'value' variable into the innerHTML of a contenteditable div enables arbitrary script injection. A red teamer could leverage this to execute payloads in the translation editor, facilitating lateral movement or privilege escalation via session hijacking.

title: X

4.name: Reflected XSS via Meta-Title Component
4.vuln: Failure to encode the title component's value allows for the injection of arbitrary HTML tags. An attacker can craft a malicious URL that, when viewed by an admin, executes scripts to exfiltrate CSRF tokens or session data.

5.name: Client-Side Script Injection in SERP Preview
5.vuln: The description field accepts unsanitized input that is rendered directly in the SERP preview UI. This primitive can be exploited to perform a DOM-based XSS attack, potentially hijacking the administrative interface.
